state.task: Implement the frontend detail and integrated English/Dutch text in the real CanLang draft files. The deciding requirements are easy adoption, economical source tokens, unchanged business behavior and a single canonical mechanism for each SaaS primitive; optimizing for people writing the source is outside the goal. The preceding requirements work calls for a built-in left sidebar that collapses, puts branding above automatically obtained page destinations and anchors account controls below, plus a sectioned settings dialog. App wrapper files, authored build inventories, additional catalogs, repeated authentication/team definitions and restated operation contracts are prohibited.
state.evidence: Across the 42 draft files there are 83 pages, 114 forms, 86 tables and 115 lists; neither card/details grouping nor explicit nav has been authored. Of those pages, 80 can be static navigation entries and three depend on context. All 39 app requirements documents now describe their particular layouts and useful personal settings. The current grammar already handles responsive cards, details rendered as Collapse, generated drawers for mutation forms, typed record collections and filters, bindings to actions and automatically produced HTMX regions. Missing facilities are personal preferences, tab selection, split views of a chosen row, selection for detail drawers and initial filter values. The corpus includes 361 descriptions and 85 explicit presentation strings, alongside 1288 fields owned by models/contracts, 461 parameters of user operations, 184 such operations and 338 enum members declared directly. A cautious shared-caption vocabulary covers 376 fields and 123 parameters; counting declarations alone does not show which surfaces users actually see. Only a syntax parser exists here: execution of rendering, resolution and BDD examples is not implemented.
state.research: The Drawer, Modal and Tab components in daisyUI supply CSS and markup building blocks. Dialog/tab guidance from WAI-ARIA assigns keyboard, focus and selection responsibilities, and HTMX needs configured swaps for error responses. Rails i18n offers an example of shared translations for schema attributes. These references establish neither the correctness of a CanLang runtime nor its automatic captions. The existing localization path remains owned messages in source, typed ICU descriptors, #= metadata, pure exports and explicit outbound format(message,locale=null). Text stored as business or user content stays untranslated.
state.preferences: The candidate adds the unnamed Given declaration preferences {fields}, limited to one instance in a logical owner. Fields may be typed scalars, enums or nullable record references whose use is authorized; a field that cannot be null must specify a constant default. No array, file, secret, action, object or nested-schema field is admitted. Built-in account, language, appearance and security controls stay shared rather than becoming copied preference fields. Persistence is restricted to the authenticated principal's own values for the selected app and team context. The runtime derives settings inputs and canonical save/reset behavior, checks values both when saved and when consumed, and verifies current access to any referenced record. Anonymous rendering takes the declared defaults. Pure checks use the existing require preferences: row... form. Access through preferences.field is confined to Then display, authorized choices of UI reads and preference checking: it cannot determine authority, business guards or transitions, persisted business fields or scheduling. When a record reference loses its grant, the runtime ignores or resets it safely and explains the fallback. Each extension field must be consumed by an actual view. This design adds neither authored preference CRUD nor a business-facing MCP operation. Identify stored extensions by (user,selected app,canonical owner,current team or none). Include each canonical owner once in a composed settings dialog, and continue sharing the base account settings.
state.ui: Retain the present groups and the sole canonical forms. list/table gain display=split to show one selected authorized record in an adjacent pane, with a drawer on mobile and unchanged row bindings. details gains display=drawer and open=boolean presentation expression while retaining enclosing scope; without the new display value it continues to use Collapse. Every collection can initialize its declared filters with defaults={filter=preferences.field}. A defaults key must be listed in filter; URL values and current controls take precedence, null imposes no initial narrowing, and current policy still applies. Introduce tabs with an optional selector for an enum preference. The leaf tabs preferences.view obtains captions from its enum members and passes the chosen value to existing UI reads; a block instead uses tab enum_case children to bind panels to distinct exact members. Without a preference binding, tabs requires captioned tab suites and keeps selection transient. It cannot write business enum fields. The extension admits no charts, drag/drop, arbitrary HTML, polling helpers or additional query helpers. Navigation comes from accessible static pages in source order; dynamic detail routes do not enter it. Authors specify genuine exceptions with page-local nav=none or order=int, and can use group=caption when a different grouping is needed. A composition renders a single shell. Removing a destination from view conveys no permission. Eliminate authored nav/link trees: deriving destinations from pages, with exceptions attached to those pages, is the only navigation mechanism. There are no corpus nav declarations needing migration. Only Collapse details accepts open; a drawer is activated for the single chosen or opened record. Choosing a bound tab immediately invokes the existing canonical preference save, including version checks; a failure is shown and the last accepted selection is reinstated, rather than adding a second writer. An enum-bound tab block must include each enum member exactly once.
state.localization: Retain the existing per-owner messages table and provide English source cells with Dutch variants. Extend its canonical for binding with comma-separated targets so an identical complete caption can label multiple owned declarations; repeated targets and targets belonging to other owners are still invalid. for package may label the owner, for preferences may label the settings section, and bindings may also address preference fields and enum members. The runtime pins one finite vocabulary keyed by field/parameter identifiers and types, plus ordinary verbs and boolean captions. It must not derive words by splitting identifiers, translate from English automatically, or alter machine identifiers. The examined vocabulary is name,title,description,body,subject,reason,notes,instructions,evidence,reference,phone,address:text; email,timezone,currency:their scalar; quantity,count:int/decimal; active,enabled,done:bool; amount,price,total:money; duration:duration; at,occurred,created_at,updated_at:datetime; due:date/datetime; revision:int; file:file. A default caption for location applies exclusively to text and to the exact shared Location symbol. A parameter whose name matches its referenced model, differing only in initial-letter case, reuses that owner's model caption; a renamed meaning requires an authored binding. Enum semantics receive no inference except boolean meanings. Remaining exposed schema, operation and role captions, domain enum captions, layout wording and descriptions stay authored explicitly. An exported schema includes its captions and pure message dependencies. Literal outbound notices become typed patterns formatted explicitly with the app default; stored dynamic notices continue as data. Whether a custom capability accepts human text must be declared against its exact pinned signature, never inferred merely because a parameter is named message. The proposed pinned verb set is submit,cancel,assign,reopen,complete,publish,pause,resume,refresh.
state.alternatives: One unnamed preferences declaration computes its identity and saves repeated naming, at the cost of restricting an owner to one extension schema and reserving that contextual syntax. Named preferences adds explicit names/references and supports several groups, increasing both tokens and the surface of state. Standard own-user models keep ordinary CRUD but require copied schemas/account integration and create another personal-settings path. A small reviewed label vocabulary saves repeated common bindings while demanding pinned versioned meanings and possible semantic overrides. Authoring every caption keeps wording visible individually but repeats standard text. Normalizing arbitrary identifiers into labels and translations minimizes authored volume while leaving domain names ambiguous and generated language less stable. A grouped for binding shares complete wording and consequently needs validation of its target list.

preference_shape.instructions: Select the personal-extension declaration approach that most closely satisfies the given source-level and runtime requirements.

criteria.unnamed: Adopt a single owner-local preferences schema with computed identity, runtime save/reset and presentation-restricted consumption; retain the one-schema limit.
criteria.named: Allow named groups of personal fields with explicit references under identical validation and ownership restrictions; retain the additional naming and group count.
criteria.ordinary_model: Represent personal fields with ordinary own-user models, CRUD and settings bindings, requiring authored schemas and account integration.
criteria.unresolved: Leave declaration shape open when every offered approach violates a supplied requirement.

label_policy.instructions: Choose the caption policy that reconciles reliable complete localization with the corpus's limits on repetition.

criteria.finite_defaults: Version the specified exact identifier/type captions and caption reuse by type; declare domain-specific meanings and overrides in source.
criteria.explicit_labels: Bind every caption explicitly to its owner, including common repeated captions, sharing complete messages where appropriate.
criteria.generic_inference: Normalize or infer arbitrary identifier wording into captions and translations, tolerating uncertainty about domain meaning.
criteria.unresolved: Keep the caption policy undecided if none of these approaches makes coverage predictable.

ui_boundary.instructions: Under the proposed rules, do preferences, tabs, default filters and record-detail presentation stay within the UI while canonical operations and current row/field grants remain intact?

criteria.true: These specified constraints uphold the boundary and introduce no other means of authorizing or writing business state.
criteria.false: At least one specified constraint allows, or fails to resolve, another route to business mutation or authorization.

grouped_labels.instructions: Can the existing for mechanism coherently bind one complete meaning to multiple owned targets while retaining typed localization owned in source and avoiding duplicated contracts?

criteria.true: Applying the extension preserves ownership and uniqueness of targets, complete-message semantics and the canonical binding contract.
criteria.false: Applying the extension violates those requirements or leaves an additional binding route unresolved.
